issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a function named `_make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None` (leading underscore), but both the template and the solution define the function as `make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None` (no underscore). This name mismatch between the specification and the provided code is structural and can confuse students about which function to implement and which tests will run.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function name consistent across the problem statement, template, and tests. Either (a) update the problem statement to refer to `make_y_state(...)` (no underscore), or (b) add a wrapper/alias in the template such as `def _make_y_state(...): return make_y_state(...)` so that both names are available. Ensure the tests reference the same name.

issues.description: The problem statement asks students to implement a function named `_make_y_state(...)`, but both the template and the solution implement the function as `make_y_state(...)` (no leading underscore). This mismatch between the documented function name and the actual code identifiers can confuse students about which function to implement or test against.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent identifier for the Y-state preparation function across all artifacts. Either update the problem statement to reference `make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None` (preferred), or rename the template/solution implementations to `_make_y_state(...)` so the name matches the problem text and tests.
